A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FoD research. Text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–C are readable, and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments on four image-restoration datasets and CIFAR-10, including sampling and noise-injection ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds image-to-image translation results, further comparisons and training-loss diagnostics.

M1.justification: The FoD SDE, architecture, training loss and Algorithms 1–4 are retained. The deterministic and alpha-free possibilities were already described in v1; their additional evaluation and revised explanation do not establish a new method.

E1.justification: Section 4.2 adds edges-to-handbags, edges-to-shoes, facades-to-labels, aerial-photos-to-maps and night-to-day translation. These substantially extend task requirements beyond degradation removal. All four restoration datasets and CIFAR-10 remain, with unconditional generation moved to Appendix C.3.

E2.justification: GOUB is newly evaluated on all four restoration datasets in Table 1. SDEdit is newly compared with FoD and Rectified Flow on handbags in Table 6. GOUB and SDEdit were cited but not evaluated in v1; existing comparator methods are retained.

E3.justification: New translation experiments use 64×64 images and include MSE evaluation in Table 6. CIFAR-10 adds 1,000-step sampling and a DDPM control using the authors' architecture and hyperparameters. Previously stated restoration splits and training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds training-checkpoint diagnostics of the Taylor approximation underlying the loss (Table 4), noise-injection ablations across four translation tasks (Table 5), and CIFAR-10 sampling-step and alpha comparisons (Figure 8). Existing restoration ablations and sampling-sensitivity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. V2's approximation-error measurements diagnose the training-loss approximation rather than uncertainty in experimental outcomes.

E6.justification: V2 adds GOUB, translation, approximation-error and CIFAR-10 result entries, including FIDs of 4.60 and 4.33 for the 1,000-step ODE and alpha-free variants. Most matched restoration scores remain unchanged, but LOL 10-step MC FID changes from 42.37 in v1 Table 1 to 32.37 in v2 Table 2. Noise-free SSIM entries are omitted.

T1.justification: Section 3.4 revises the stated exact flow-matching reduction: v1 permits constant alpha=1, whereas v2 specifies linear decay from 1 to 0. The core FoD solution, log-normal corollary and appendix derivations remain unchanged; the new interpolant expression largely rearranges the existing solution.

C1.justification: The central forward-only, tractability and fast-sampling claims remain. The abstract changes its empirical claim from competitive conditional and unconditional generation to state-of-the-art restoration and qualitative translation capability. The introduction and conclusion adopt this revised emphasis.

C2.justification: Appendix A.3 newly explains that the loss serves as a surrogate early in training when the Taylor approximation fails. Section 5 qualifies fast-sampling gains as PSNR improvements and adds specific future directions involving log-space transformations, transport paths and schedules. The unconditional-generation weakness was already discussed in v1.

D1.justification: Sections 4.2 and C.1 document translation dataset sources, 64×64 preprocessing and reuse of restoration settings. Existing optimizer, learning rate, hardware, training duration, restoration splits and code-access statement remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 3.4 explicitly positions FoD as an instantiation of stochastic interpolants, expanding the earlier related-work connection. Added references include Pix2Pix, BBDM and residual denoising diffusion models. The broader diffusion and flow-matching positioning is retained.

P1.justification: Retained material is substantially reorganized: Section 3.4 becomes Connection to Prior Work, unconditional experiments move to Appendix C.3, and Section 5 and Appendix C are restructured. The abstract, introduction and conclusion are revised, alongside citation-style and affiliation changes.

P2.justification: The restoration table is reorganized into Tables 1–3, and translation and diagnostic displays are added. The CIFAR comparison and full training curves move to the appendix, while diffusion visualizations gain translation examples. Figure 2 also reorders FoD columns and incorrectly reverses the GT/LQ labels.

improvement.justification: The translation experiments and additional comparisons broaden empirical validation, while Appendix A.3 explains the training-loss approximation's limitations more clearly. These provide a modest improvement in support and transparency, outweighing the new GT/LQ label error in Figure 2 and reduced SSIM ablation reporting.
